source_text: Quae definitio ad intellegendam quoque iustitiam Dei aperuit viam, ut censeremus aequitatem divini neutiquam stare iudicii, nisi illud imputasset in peccatum, a quo nosset liberum fuisse ei, qui propter hoc affligitur, abstinere.
pass_a_gloss: Which definition also opened a way toward understanding the justice of God, so that we judged that the equity of the divine judgment in no way stands, unless it had imputed into sin that from which it knew it had been free for him who is afflicted on account of this to abstain.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS abstineo; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: This definition also opened the way to understanding God’s justice. We could judge that the fairness of divine judgment could never stand unless God imputed as sin only an act from which he knew the person punished for it had been free to abstain.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
